newsitem.title: GERMANY: Thyssen steel unit Q1 sales fall 19 pct.
newsitem.headline: Thyssen steel unit Q1 sales fall 19 pct.

text.p: Thyssen Stahl AG, Germany's largest steel maker, said on Thursday its sales in the first quarter of 1996/97 were down 19 percent to 2.1 billion marks.
Despite that decline and a sharp drop in 1995/96 profit, the steel unit of Thyssen AG said the steel business was back on an uptrend.

Thyssen Stahl chairman Ekkehard Schulz said he shared the view of the Wirtschaftsvereinigung Stahl industry group that German crude steel production should rise five percent to nearly 42 million tonnes in 1997.

Domestic steel consumption should rise 2.5 percent due to satisfactory capacity utilisation for steel customers. Crude steel production in the European Union should rise four percent to 154 million tonnes, he said.
"The negative portion of the inventory cycle has been overcome," he said. "We hold these projections for realistic."
Earlier, Thyssen Stahl reported that 1995/96 net profit dropped to 174 million marks from 651 million marks, as sales declined to 10.623 billion marks from 11.937 billion marks.
